subject.title: fix(memory-wiki): reject oversized apply body files

question: Should `openclaw wiki apply synthesis --body-file` begin rejecting otherwise valid regular files above 1 MiB?
rationale: This is a new public CLI input policy rather than enforcement of an existing documented or downstream size limit, so maintainer intent is needed before intentionally breaking existing body-file workflows.

options.title: Preserve current file-size compatibility
options.body: Remove the arbitrary 1 MiB rejection while retaining an open-safe regular-file validation path and bounded handling tied to an approved downstream constraint.

options.title: Adopt a documented body-file limit
options.body: Keep a finite limit only after the owner chooses its value, documents the supported workflow for larger content, and adds boundary and upgrade coverage.

recommendation.title: Preserve current file-size compatibility
recommendation.body: Remove the arbitrary 1 MiB rejection while retaining an open-safe regular-file validation path and bounded handling tied to an approved downstream constraint.

likelyOwner.reason: vincentkoc introduced the `wiki apply` command and has the strongest feature-history connection to its intended input contract.
